# Code scout

Answers one question about one repository's code. You edit nothing and you search nowhere else.

You are given the repository's absolute path, the question, and optionally context on why it is being asked and whether test files are in scope (they are not by default).

## Read the layout first

Read the repository's `CLAUDE.md` or `README.md` when one exists, for how the code is laid out and what the parts are called. Use those names in your search patterns and target the directories they point at.

## Depth

The wording of the question tells you how deep to go.

- "Where", "find", "locate", "definition": find the thing, return it.
- "How", "flow", "calls", "uses": find it and trace what calls it and what it calls, far enough to answer.
- "End to end", "complete", "trace", "understand": follow the whole path and report each step.

When in doubt, go deeper. Missing a connection costs the caller a second dispatch.

## Scope

Only the repository you were given. Use `git -C <repo-path>` and absolute paths for everything; never `cd`. When the answer points outside the repository (an import from another package, a call to another service, a table another codebase owns), report the reference and where it points, and search nothing beyond the boundary.

## Output

Lead with the answer to the question in one to three sentences. Then the findings that support it, each with `path:line` (or `path:start-end`), one line on why it matters, and a snippet only when the code itself is the answer, trimmed to the lines that carry it. Verify every line number against the file before reporting it.

Then, only when they exist: references that leave the repository, and what you searched for and did not find.

Keep the whole report under forty lines. Long reports get cut in delivery. Report what is there; when nothing matches, say so and list the patterns you tried.

## Task

Repository: /home/agus/workspace/asermax/nagara

Question (end to end): how does nagara manage an item and its voice today, from enqueue to the audio a client plays? We are preparing to support two TTS models (Kokoro and Phonon), each with its own voices, so trace everything that touches the voice or would need to know the model.

Report:
- The item row in `common/src/db/schema.ts`: every column, which are about voice/audio/TTS, constraints and defaults; the cost ledger table(s) related to TTS.
- `api/`: the enqueue route's request body (voice param, validation), `api/src/voices.ts` (the curated list, `pickVoice`, how an unknown voice is handled), what the poll/get route returns about voice and audio, the retry route, any route that lists voices. Response types from `common/`.
- `pipeline/`: where the item Workflow reads the voice, the synthesis steps, `pipeline/src/tts/modal.ts` (request/response, the URLs and secrets it is configured with), the cost entry (`ttsDollarsPerSecond`), and config in `pipeline/wrangler.jsonc` about TTS.
- `tts/app.py`: the `StartRequest` voice default, the class, the endpoints (briefly; a previous scout covered it).
- Anything else carrying the voice or a model name: tests' fixtures, types in `common/`.

You may go up to 80 lines. Write the report to /home/agus/workspace/asermax/nagara/.scratch/phonon-spike/scout-voice-flow.md, then reply with only that path.
</supervisor-agent>

# Voice flow, enqueue to audio (nagara @ a2a68b1)

Answer: the voice is one free-text string. The client may send it to `POST /items`, and the API stores it in `items.voice` (NOT NULL, no default, no CHECK). The pipeline passes it unchanged to Modal's `/start`. No model name exists anywhere: not in the schema, the API, the pipeline request, the cost ledger or the config. The model is hard-wired to Kokoro in `tts/app.py`. No route lists voices.

## common/ schema
- `common/src/db/schema.ts:50-79` `items` columns: id (`itm`), url, title?, **voice text NOT NULL (:58)**, status (enum + CHECK), created_at, updated_at, queued_at, workflow_instance_id?, current_step?, extraction_domain?, recipe_version_id? (FK), retry_count int default 0, **duration real? (:68), audio_format text? (:69)**, units JSON?, degradations JSON?, error?. Checks: status, units/degradations json_valid.
- Audio-written columns: duration, audio_format, units (timings merged in). There is no TTS model, sample rate or provider column.
- `schema.ts:81-105` `cost_entries`: id (`cst`), item_id FK, type CHECK in (firecrawl, describer, tts), quantity real, unit CHECK in (credits, calls, seconds), dollars real, cached bool default false, detail JSON?, created_at. Index on item_id.
- `common/src/ledger.ts:3-17` defines COST_TYPE/COST_UNIT. The DB has only the initial migration, `common/migrations/0000_initial.sql` (voice at :23, type CHECK at :12).
- `common/src/db/items/create-item.ts:5-8` `createItem(db,{url,voice})` inserts status queued.
- `common/src/db/operations/record-audio.ts:10-24` batch: sets units/duration/audio_format, status ready, and inserts the cost entry.
- `ItemRow = typeof items.$inferSelect` (`common/src/item.ts:12`), so the voice type is `string`.

## api/
- `api/src/routes/enqueue.ts:7-10` valibot body `{url: string, voice?: string}`. Any string is accepted; a wrong shape gives 400 "the body needs a url string and an optional voice string" (:24). `voice: pickVoice(parsed.output.voice)` at :30.
- `api/src/voices.ts:3-17` VOICE_POOL of 10 Kokoro ids (af_heart, af_bella, af_sarah, af_sky, af_aoede, af_alloy, af_nova, am_fenrir, am_michael, am_puck). `pickVoice(voice)` returns `voice ?? random pool entry`. An unknown voice is never validated or rejected; it is stored and fails later in Modal.
- `api/src/response.ts:8-23` `toItemResponse` returns id, url, title, status, voice, created_at, duration and units (only when ready), error, and `audio_url` (`/items/{id}/audio`, only when ready). It returns no model, format or `audio_format`. The response type is inferred; there is no named type in `common/`.
- `api/src/routes/poll.ts` GET item: `requeueIfStale` then `toItemResponse`. `api/src/routes/audio.ts:5-13` 404 unless ready and `audio_format` is set, else a signed redirect to `audioKey(id)`. The format is not used for Content-Type there.
- `api/src/routes/retry.ts:14-58` `claimRetry`, then restart the Workflow. The voice is kept because the row is reused. A retry cannot change the voice.
- Routes (`api/src/index.ts`): enqueue, poll, retry, audio, images, `/health`. No voices-list route.

## pipeline/
- `pipeline/src/workflow/steps/synthesis.ts:26-37` `startSynthesisStep` reads the item and sends `{paragraphs: units.map(u=>u.spoken), voice: item.voice, destination: presigned PUT URL}` (:30-34). The destination is a single `audioKey(itemId)`.
- `synthesis.ts:41-52` `waitForSynthesisStep` polls `synthesisResult` every `pollIntervalSeconds`.
- `synthesis.ts:57-85` `storeStep` checks that the timing count equals the unit count (NonRetryable otherwise), then `recordAudio`. The cost entry is `{type:"tts", quantity: duration, unit:"seconds", dollars: duration * env.ttsDollarsPerSecond, detail:{duration}}`. Neither voice nor model is in `detail`.
- `pipeline/src/tts/modal.ts:3-14` types: `SynthesisResult {ready, format "audio/ogg"|"audio/wav", duration, timings[]}` and `SynthesisRequest {paragraphs, voice, destination}`. :22-34 POST `MODAL_START_URL` returns `call_id`. :38-60 GET `MODAL_RESULT_URL?call_id=`: 202 not ready, 410/422 NonRetryable, other non-ok retryable. Auth headers `Modal-Key`/`Modal-Secret` from `MODAL_PROXY_KEY`/`MODAL_PROXY_SECRET` (secrets, `.dev.vars.example:7-8`).
- `pipeline/wrangler.jsonc:40-41` MODAL_START_URL/MODAL_RESULT_URL = `https://asermax--nagara-tts-web.modal.run/{start,result}` (one app, one model); :48 `ttsDollarsPerSecond: 0.000015` (a single global rate). Dev URLs: `pipeline/.dev.vars.example:21-22`. R2_UPLOAD_ENDPOINT/R2_S3_ENDPOINT/R2_BUCKET also feed the upload URL.

## tts/app.py
- :1 docstring "Kokoro-82M on Modal". `StartRequest` (:32-35) `{paragraphs, voice="af_heart", destination}`; the default exists only here.
- :26 `SR = 24000`, :27 `PAUSE_S = 0.1` (both global constants). `synthesize_to` (:94-132) runs `pipeline(para, voice=voice)` per paragraph, joins the audio with gaps, and encodes Opus 24k mono (WAV fallback, :73-91). It PUTs to `destination` and returns format, duration and timings.
- :135-138 `_bake` warm-up with `KPipeline(lang_code="a")`, voice af_heart. `lang_code="a"` is American English only, while the `b*` voices ("bf_emma" in tests) need `"b"`.
- :160 `class Kokoro` (L4 GPU, snapshot) with `load()` and `synthesize()`. :180-185 POST `/start` calls `Kokoro().synthesize.spawn`; :188-206 GET `/result`; :209 `web` ASGI app. The class name and the app name `nagara-tts` are tied to Kokoro.

## Tests and fixtures carrying the voice
- `api/test/enqueue.test.ts:6` duplicates the VOICE_POOL; :22-57 test the requested voice (`bf_emma`) and the pool pick.
- Fixtures with `af_heart`: `api/test/helpers/items.ts:15`, `api/test/poll.test.ts:43`, `common/test/db/insert-item.ts:15`, `common/test/db/create-item.test.ts:15`, `common/test/db/get-item.test.ts:19`, `pipeline/test/helpers/item.ts:18` (default param).
- `pipeline/test/helpers/services.ts:136-175` Modal fake (starts record `voice`); `pipeline/test/item-workflow.test.ts:118-127` asserts the start voice and headers; `item-synthesis.test.ts` covers the failure paths. Cost tests: `common/test/db/create-cost-entry.test.ts`, `record-audio.test.ts:21`.

## Docs (not read)
Voice/Kokoro is mentioned in `docs/technical-design/{tts-service,item-contract,item-lifecycle,persistence-and-storage,article-extraction}.md` and `docs/product-design/{queue,what-gets-read-aloud,what-nagara-is}.md`.

## Not found
No model field or column, no voice validation, no voices endpoint, no per-model config or cost rate, no model name in cost `detail`.
EOF
